description: Mass-bias sign equation for strong-field Phantom Mass
central_question: Do slow deep clocks produce inflated or deflated inferred mass?
naive_argument: Slow clocks alone (S_a=1, D_dyn=1) give M_app = M_local / T_P^2 < M_local (DEFLATION)

sources: 1. Lensing magnification: temporal field bends photon paths (S_a > 1)
2. Distance miscalibration: GR-inferred distance differs from true (S_a ≠ 1)
3. Orbital dynamics: modified effective potential changes local orbit

critical_threshold.example: For T_P = 10: S_a > 4.64, mu > 21.5 (strong but achievable near compact object)

spatial_calibration.key_point: The spatial calibration is NOT a free parameter — it is determined by the photon propagation on tilde_g and the orbital dynamics on the temporal-well geometry

outcome_1.name: Positive Phantom Mass
outcome_1.interpretation: Spatial magnification dominates temporal stretching. The conventional mass is inflated. M_matter < M_GR-fit.
outcome_1.implication: The compact-object mass contains a temporal-inference component. Strong-field Phantom Mass is real.

outcome_2.name: Zero Phantom Mass
outcome_2.interpretation: Spatial and temporal effects exactly cancel. The conventional mass equals the local material mass.
outcome_2.implication: TEP reduces to GR for mass inference. No Phantom Mass at black-hole scales.

outcome_3.name: Negative Phantom Mass
outcome_3.interpretation: Temporal stretching dominates. The conventional mass is deflated. M_matter > M_GR-fit.
outcome_3.implication: Slow deep clocks make the inferred mass smaller. The object has MORE material mass than GR suggests.

three_outcomes.key_principle: The pipeline must be allowed to return any of the three outcomes. A pipeline structured to only return outcome_1 is not testing the thesis — it is confirming it.

conclusion: The sign is determined by the competition between spatial magnification and temporal stretching. It is testable, not assumed.
